chunks: Should We treat those who submit and obey in the same way as those who are culpable?

key_terms.الْمُجْرِمِينَ: The criminals, those who commit sins
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمِينَ: The believers, those who submit to God

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Should We treat those who submit and obey in the same way as those who are culpable?'
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this rhetorical question from Surah Al-Qalam underscores the principle of *Adl* (Divine Justice), affirming that God does not arbitrarily equate the *Mu'minun* (believers) with the *Mujrimun* (sinners). It highlights the distinct spiritual stations of the righteous, particularly the Ahl al-Bayt and the Imams, who are purified from sin, contrasting them with those who reject divine guidance. This verse serves as a foundational proof for the merit of the faithful and the reality of individual accountability in the Hereafter.
